title: Affine-chart comparison of geometric and algebraic strict local rings
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $i:\operatorname{Spec}D\hookrightarrow X$ be an affine open immersion [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], and let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] with image $x$ in this open. Let $\mathfrak p\subset D$ be the prime corresponding to $x$, identify $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $K\subset\Omega$ be its separable algebraic closure inside $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. Put $L=D_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and choose an algebraic strict henselization $L^{\mathrm{sh}}$ relative to $K$ with a defining pointed-etale colimit cocone and its induced residue map to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Let $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ be the chosen affine pointed-neighbourhood ring colimit and $X_{(\bar x)}=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with structural morphism $\rho:X_{(\bar x)}\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Give $C$ its $D$-algebra structure through the colimit leg for the uniquely lifted geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}D$. There is a $D$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:C\xrightarrow{\sim}L^{\mathrm{sh}}$ such that
$$\rho\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\theta)=i\circ\operatorname{Spec}(D\to L\to L^{\mathrm{sh}}).$$
Both $C$ and $L^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are strictly henselian local rings [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. The induced residue map $\psi:L^{\mathrm{sh}}\to K$ is surjective with kernel the maximal ideal of $L^{\mathrm{sh}}$, and $\psi\circ\theta$, followed by the inclusion $K\subset\Omega$, equals the canonical geometric-point evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_{\bar x}:C\to\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-point-evaluation]. Hence $\mathrm{ev}_{\bar x}$ has image $K$ and kernel the maximal ideal of $C$, identifying the residue field of $C$ with $K$, and under these identifications the residue-field isomorphism induced by $\theta$ is the identity of $K$.

source.place: Tag 04HX, label lemma-describe-etale-local-ring, statement and proof: affine neighbourhood, residue triples and comparison with the algebraic strict henselization; algebra.tex Tag 04GW, label lemma-strict-henselization-different, for the algebraic colimit model.

proof.text: Write $H=L^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $a:L\to H$ for its given structural map. The open immersion identifies the chart with an open subscheme, so $\bar x$ lifts uniquely to $\bar x_D:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}D$: its one-point source has image in that open, and its sheaf map restricts there. Its residue embedding is the specified $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\Omega$. By the relative-separable-closure statement, $K$ is a separable closure of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=L/\mathfrak pL$. Denote the resulting evaluation by $r:L\to K$. Keep this very field and embedding throughout.

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring, first paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 04GW, lemma-strict-henselization-different

proof.text: Apply the affine-neighbourhood/triples comparison with $Y=X$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$, and $\kappa(\bar x)=K$. It identifies the chosen ring $C$, with its colimit legs, with the colimit of $D$-etale residue triples $t=(B_t,q_t,\phi_t)$ over $(\mathfrak p,K)$. Write $c_t:B_t\to C$ for the transported legs and $e_t:B_t\to K$ for their pointed evaluations. The identity triple $t_0=(D,\mathfrak p,\kappa(\mathfrak p)\hookrightarrow K)$ has a morphism to every triple, namely its structural map $\alpha_t:D\to B_t$; hence $c_t\alpha_t=c_{t_0}=b:D\to C$. Compatibility with the chart neighbourhood leg identifies $b$ with the $D$-algebra map required in the statement. All colimits here and below are taken on small representative categories: the chosen neighbourhood-colimit definition and the pointed-algebra definition provide these representatives, and the chart equivalence preserves the colimit legs.

Apply the strict-henselization-triples theorem to this $D$-triple colimit. It makes $C$ strictly henselian local and supplies a surjection $\epsilon:C\to K$ with $\ker\epsilon=\mathfrak m_C=\mathfrak pC$ and $\epsilon c_t=e_t$. On every neighbourhood over the chart, inclusion $j:K\hookrightarrow\Omega$ composed with $e_t$ is exactly its geometric-point evaluation, by the pointed-neighbourhood/triple correspondence. Thus $j\epsilon$ and $\mathrm{ev}_{\bar x}$ agree on those neighbourhood legs. Their equality on $C$ follows from the canonical chart-colimit identification and the defining universal property of the evaluation map. In particular $\epsilon b$ is the original evaluation $D\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to K$.

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring; algebra.tex Tags 04GP and 04GW, lemma-strict-henselization and lemma-strict-henselization-different

proof.text: Use the defining pointed-etale $L$-algebra cocone $d_u:S_u\to H$ chosen in the statement; write $v_u:S_u\to K$ for its pointing. We need its specified residue map, not one from an unrelated cocone. Convert a local-base residue triple $(S,q,\phi)$ to the pointed algebra $(S,\phi\circ\mathrm{ev}_q)$. Conversely, the field-spectrum correspondence applied to $v:S\to K$ gives $q=\ker v$ and the unique embedding $\phi:\kappa(q)\to K$ factoring $v$. Since $v$ restricts to $r$ on $L$, $q$ lies over $\mathfrak pL$. These operations are inverse on objects up to the canonical identity of the ring, and on morphisms they retain the same ring map: the pointing equation is precisely the residue-triple equation. They preserve the $L$-maps and every evaluation into $K$. Therefore the given legs $d_u$ form a universal ring cocone for the local-base triples as well: a competing ring cocone pulls back to the pointed-algebra diagram. Its leg at $(L,r)$ equips its vertex with an $L$-algebra structure; the arrows from $(L,r)$ to all objects make every leg $L$-linear. It therefore descends uniquely by the defining algebra-colimit property, and the inverse construction proves factorization and uniqueness on the triples. The induced map to $K$ is exactly the given $\psi:H\to K$, since on each given leg it equals $v_u$.

source.place: Tag 04GW, lemma-strict-henselization-different, pointed-algebra interpretation of the local-base triples

proof.text: Apply the strict-henselization-triples theorem over the local ring $L$, at its maximal ideal $\mathfrak pL$, with the same separable closure $K$, to the cocone of the preceding step. It makes $H$ strictly henselian local, and its compatible evaluation map is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak m_H$. This compatible evaluation is $\psi$ by its equations on the defining legs, so $\psi$ has exactly these properties and $\psi a=r$.

For $s\in D\setminus\mathfrak p$, the value $\epsilon(b(s))$ is nonzero, so $b(s)\notin\mathfrak m_C$ and the local-ring unit criterion makes $b(s)$ a unit. The localization universal property gives a unique $b_L:L=D_{\mathfrak p}\to C$ extending $b$. The maps $\epsilon b_L$ and $r:L\to K$ agree on $D$, and hence are equal by uniqueness for localization. Thus $C$, with the specified residue evaluation, is now an $L$-algebra over exactly the chosen $L\to K$.

source.place: Tag 00E9, lemma-characterize-local-ring; localization universal property, as used in the comparison of Tag 04GW

proof.text: For each defining pointed-etale $L$-algebra $(S_u,v_u)$ of $H$, apply the unique henselian ring lifting lemma with base $R=L$, target $S=C$, base map $b_L$, residue surjection $\epsilon$, and prescribed map $v_u:S_u\to K$. Its compatibility hypothesis is $v_u|_L=r=\epsilon b_L$. Obtain a unique $f_u:S_u\to C$ with $f_u|_L=b_L$ and $\epsilon f_u=v_u$. If $\beta:S_u\to S_w$ is a pointed transition, both $f_w\beta$ and $f_u$ meet these same two equations; the uniqueness clause identifies them. The defining colimit therefore gives $f:H\to C$ with $fd_u=f_u$. Evaluate on the identity pointed algebra $L$ to obtain $fa=b_L$; evaluate on every $d_u$ to obtain $\epsilon f=\psi$.

source.place: Tag 08HQ, lemma-map-into-henselian, followed by the defining colimit universal property

proof.text: For each $D$-triple $t$, apply the same lifting lemma with base $R=D$, target $S=H$, base map $D\to L\xrightarrow{a}H$, residue surjection $\psi$, and prescribed map $e_t:B_t\to K$. The compatibility holds because both restrictions to $D$ are the geometric-point evaluation. Obtain a unique $g_t:B_t\to H$ with these base and residue equations. For every triple transition $\beta:B_t\to B_w$, uniqueness identifies $g_w\beta$ with $g_t$. The $D$-triple colimit of step 2 gives $g:C\to H$ satisfying $gc_t=g_t$. At $t_0$ its base equation is $gb=a\circ(D\to L)$; colimit extensionality gives $\psi g=\epsilon$. Moreover $gb_L=a$ as maps $L\to H$, since they agree on $D$ and localization uniqueness applies.

source.place: Tag 08HQ, lemma-map-into-henselian; Tag 04GW, lemma-strict-henselization-different, colimit comparison

proof.text: For each $D$-triple $t$, the maps $fgc_t$ and $c_t:B_t\to C$ have the same structural $D$-map $b$, and $\epsilon fgc_t=\psi gc_t=e_t=\epsilon c_t$. The uniqueness clause of the henselian lifting lemma gives $fgc_t=c_t$, so $fg=\mathrm{id}_C$ by colimit extensionality. For each defining $L$-etale algebra $S_u$, the maps $gfd_u$ and $d_u:S_u\to H$ have the same structural $L$-map $a$ (use $gb_L=a$), and $\psi gfd_u=\epsilon fd_u=v_u=\psi d_u$. The same uniqueness clause gives $gfd_u=d_u$, so $gf=\mathrm{id}_H$. Set $\theta=g$ with inverse $f$. Its equation on $b$ makes it a $D$-algebra isomorphism, and $\psi\theta=\epsilon$.

source.place: Tag 08HQ, lemma-map-into-henselian, uniqueness on each etale stage; Tag 04GW, lemma-strict-henselization-different

proof.text: The structural-map definition evaluated at the chart neighbourhood gives $\rho=i\circ\operatorname{Spec}(b)$. Contravariance of $\operatorname{Spec}$ and $\theta b=a\circ(D\to L)$ therefore give $\rho\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\theta)=i\circ\operatorname{Spec}(D\to L\to H)$, with the claimed orientation. Both rings are strictly henselian by steps 3 and 5. Also $j\psi\theta=j\epsilon=\mathrm{ev}_{\bar x}$ by steps 3 and 9. Since $\epsilon$ and $\psi$ are surjective with maximal-ideal kernels and $j$ is an inclusion, the evaluation on $C$ has image $K$ and kernel $\mathfrak m_C$. On quotients, an element represented by $c\in C$ is identified on the two sides with $\epsilon(c)$ and $\psi(\theta(c))$ respectively; these are equal. Thus the residue-field map induced by $\theta$ is the identity of $K$ under exactly the stated identifications.
